data.name: Cli_UsageApply
data.value: M-Tool.exe --apply charge <50-100> [--confirm] M-Tool.exe --apply boost on|off [--confirm] M-Tool.exe --apply perf high|balanced|eco [--confirm] M-Tool.exe --apply fan default|cool|silent [--confirm] M-Tool.exe --apply fanmode auto|advanced [--confirm] M-Tool.exe --restore [--confirm] (factory fan table) M-Tool.exe --unlock --confirm (remove the lock left by a failed write) Without --confirm: dry run, nothing is written to the laptop. The command line ignores dryRun in settings.json; every live write needs --confirm.

data.comment: Tray submenu title. Keep the English word "Language" in the text, in every language, so a user who ended up in a language they cannot read can still find the menu.

data.name: Lang_Windows
data.comment: Choice in the tray language menu: follow the display language of Windows. The other choices are language names written in their own language and are not translated.

data.value: Language saved. It applies the next time M-Tool starts.
data.comment: Status message after a language was chosen in the tray menu. It is shown in the language that was chosen, so the user can tell it worked.

data.name: Report_Create
data.comment: Tray menu item. Creates a read-only report about this laptop (a zip with report.txt and dsdt.aml) that the user can attach to a GitHub issue. It never uses the WMI2 interface.

data.name: Report_CreateWmi2
data.comment: Tray menu item, only on newer MSI laptops that have the WMI2 interface. Like Report_Create, and it also includes the laptop's raw WMI2 answers. Asks for confirmation first (Report_Wmi2Confirm). Keep the name WMI2 and the same wording as Report_Create.

data.name: Report_OpenFolder
data.comment: Tray menu item, shown after a report was created in this session. Opens the folder with the zip in Windows Explorer.

data.name: Report_IssueMenu
data.comment: Tray menu item. Opens the GitHub page where the user sends the report as a "Device report" issue, in the web browser. Keep GitHub in the text.

data.name: Report_Working
data.value: Creating the device report. This can take a few seconds.
data.comment: Tray balloon and status message while the report is being created.

data.name: Report_Saved
data.value: Report saved: {0}. To send it, choose "{1}" in the tray menu and drag the zip file into the form.
data.comment: Tray balloon and status message after the report was created. {0} is the shortened folder (%AppData%) and the file name of the zip, never the full path with the user name; it is followed by a full stop, so the sentence about sending starts clearly. {1} is the tray item Report_IssueMenu: use its exact wording. A zip cannot be attached through the web address, so the user drags it into the form. Keep the balloon short: it is cut at 255 characters.

data.name: Report_Failed
data.value: The device report could not be created. See the log file for details.
data.comment: Warning (status message and tray balloon) when the report could not be created. It must not contain a path or a user name.

data.name: Report_TimedOut
data.value: The device report timed out. Try again; see the log file for details.
data.comment: Warning (status message and tray balloon) when creating the report did not finish in a few minutes, usually because the laptop's WMI did not answer. It must not contain a path or a user name.

data.name: Report_OpenFailed
data.value: Could not open the folder or the browser. See the log file for details.
data.comment: Warning when Windows could not open the report folder or the web browser. It must not contain a path or a user name.

data.name: Report_Wmi2Confirm
data.value:
Create a device report with the raw WMI2 answers?
M-Tool only reads. It calls a fixed list of this laptop's Get_* WMI2 methods once. Nothing is written to the laptop and nothing is changed.
report.txt will contain MSI's raw WMI2 answers as hex bytes. M-Tool cannot filter them. The report is meant for a public GitHub issue, so look through report.txt before you send it.
data.comment: SAFETY. Question in a Yes/No window before the WMI2 report. Say clearly that this only reads, that a fixed list of Get_* methods is called once, that nothing is written or changed, that the raw WMI2 answers are in report.txt as hex bytes and cannot be filtered, and that the report goes to a public GitHub issue. Keep Get_*, WMI2, report.txt and the line breaks. The answer buttons are Common_Yes and Common_No.

data.name: Report_SendEcData
data.comment: Tray menu item. Collects read-only data about this laptop, shows the full text, and sends it to the M-Tool server only if the user agrees. 'config' is M-Tool's settings file for a laptop model; keep EC as is.

data.name: Submit_Collecting
data.value: Collecting the EC data. This can take a few seconds.
data.comment: Tray balloon and status message while the data is read.

data.name: Submit_PreviewTitle
data.comment: Title of the window that shows the full text before sending.

data.name: Submit_PreviewNotice
data.value: Exactly the text below is sent, nothing else. Your user and computer names are hidden as <hidden>. Your IP address reaches Cloudflare; the M-Tool server does not store it and only uses a hash of it for one minute to limit how often data is sent. The data becomes a record in a private GitHub repository so M-Tool can learn new models.
data.comment: SAFETY. Text above the preview. Say clearly: exactly the shown text is sent and nothing else; user and computer names are replaced by <hidden>; the IP address reaches Cloudflare, the server does not store it and uses only a hash of it for one minute for the rate limit; the data goes to a private GitHub repository. Keep <hidden>, Cloudflare, M-Tool, GitHub and IP as they are.

data.name: Submit_Send
data.comment: Button in the preview window. Not the default button.

data.name: Submit_DontSend
data.comment: Button in the preview window; the default (Enter and Esc). Short.

data.name: Submit_Wmi2Confirm
data.value:
Read this laptop's WMI2 data for the submission?
M-Tool only reads. It calls a fixed list of this laptop's Get_* WMI2 methods once. Nothing is written to the laptop and nothing is changed.
Nothing is sent yet: you will see the full text first and choose whether to send it.
data.comment:
SAFETY. Yes/No question before the WMI2 data is read for the submission; No is the default. Say clearly that this only reads, that a fixed list of Get_* methods is called once, that nothing is written or changed, and that nothing is sent before the user sees the full text and chooses. Keep Get_*, WMI2, M-Tool and the line breaks (
).

data.name: Submit_Sent
data.comment: Tray balloon and status message after the server took the data. May be followed by Submit_Record.

data.name: Submit_Duplicate
data.value: This laptop's data has already arrived, thank you.
data.comment: After sending, when the server already had data for this model, firmware and BIOS. May be followed by Submit_Record.

data.name: Submit_Record
data.comment: Second sentence after Submit_Sent or Submit_Duplicate. {0} is a short code like 0123456789ab the user can quote.

data.name: Submit_RateLimited
data.value: Too many sends. Wait {0} min and try again.
data.comment: Warning. {0} is a number of minutes (1 to 60). Use the short form of 'minutes' that needs no plural.

data.name: Submit_Unavailable
data.value: The server is not accepting data right now. Try again later, or send the device report through GitHub.
data.comment: Warning when the server answered with an error or is over its daily limit.

data.name: Submit_Rejected
data.value: The server did not accept the data. Update M-Tool, or send the device report through GitHub.
data.comment: Warning when the server refused the data, usually because this M-Tool version is too old.

data.name: Submit_Network
data.value: Could not reach the server. Check the internet connection and try again.
data.comment: Warning: no network, DNS, proxy or TLS problem.

data.name: Submit_Timeout
data.value: The server did not answer. Try again later.
data.comment: Warning: no answer within 20 seconds.

data.name: Submit_TooLarge
data.value: The data is larger than expected and was not sent. Send the device report through GitHub instead.
data.comment: Warning: the data is over the size limit; nothing was sent.

data.name: ReportOnly_Title
data.comment: Title of the small window shown instead of the app on a laptop M-Tool cannot control yet.

data.name: ReportOnly_Help
data.value: You can still help: send this laptop's data so M-Tool can learn it.
data.comment: Line in that window, below the explanation of why M-Tool cannot control this laptop, above the report buttons.

data.name: Chart_Name
data.comment: Screen reader name of the fan curve chart in the editor. {0} is CPU or GPU.

data.name: Chart_PointName
data.comment: Screen reader name of a draggable point on the chart: {0} point number, {1} temperature at which the fan speeds up, {2} fan speed in percent.

data.name: Chart_IdlePointName
data.comment: Screen reader name of the first point, the speed when the laptop is cool. {0} fan speed in percent.

data.name: Chart_PointHelp
data.value: Move it with the arrow keys, by 5 with Shift. Allowed: {0}
data.comment: Screen reader help for a chart point. {0} is the allowed range, e.g. "64–71 °C, 45–65%".

data.name: Chart_AxisTemperature
data.comment: Label under the chart's horizontal axis.

data.name: Chart_AxisSpeed
data.comment: Label beside the chart's vertical axis (percent).

data.name: Chart_PercentTick
data.comment: A number on the chart's vertical axis, e.g. 60%. Put the percent sign where your language puts it.

data.name: Chart_LegendRise
data.comment: Legend for the solid line: above this temperature the fan speeds up.

data.name: Chart_LegendDown
data.comment: Legend for the dashed lines: below this temperature the fan slows back down.

data.name: Wmi2_Confirm
data.value:
Show this laptop's live values?
M-Tool only reads. While this window is open, it calls a fixed list of this laptop's Get_* WMI2 methods, at most once every 2 seconds. Nothing is written to the laptop and nothing is changed.
The values are experimental: M-Tool has not been checked on this model, so they may be wrong. Compare them with MSI Center or HWiNFO before you rely on them.
data.comment: SAFETY. Question in a Yes/No window before the live WMI2 values are read (asked once per session, No is the default). Say clearly that M-Tool only reads, that a fixed list of Get_* methods is called at most every 2 seconds while the window is open, that nothing is written or changed, and that the values are unverified and may be wrong. Keep Get_*, WMI2, MSI Center, HWiNFO and the line breaks. The answer buttons are Common_Yes and Common_No.

data.name: Wmi2_SectionTitle
data.comment: Section heading in the reports-only window on WMI2 laptops.

data.name: Wmi2_ExperimentalBand
data.value: Read-only and experimental: the values are not verified on this model. M-Tool changes nothing on this laptop.
data.comment: SAFETY. Band under Wmi2_SectionTitle, always shown. Say that it only reads, that the values are unverified and may be wrong, and that nothing is changed. Keep WMI2.

data.name: Wmi2_Show
data.comment: Button that starts reading (asks Wmi2_Confirm first).

data.name: Wmi2_Refresh
data.comment: Button: reads the values once more now.

data.name: Wmi2_Stop
data.comment: Button: stops reading the live values.

data.name: Wmi2_TryAgain
data.comment: Button shown after Wmi2_Stopped: starts reading again.

data.name: Wmi2_Stopped
data.value: Reading stopped: the laptop did not answer twice in a row. Try again, or send a device report if it keeps happening.
data.comment: Message in the live values section after two failed reads in a row; M-Tool reads nothing more until the user presses Wmi2_TryAgain.

data.name: Wmi2_ReadFailed
data.value: The laptop did not answer; the values shown may be out of date.
data.comment: Message in the live values section after one failed read.

data.name: Wmi2_Unavailable
data.value: The WMI2 interface could not be opened; see the log file for details.
data.comment: Message in the live values section when the interface cannot be opened. Keep WMI2.

data.name: Wmi2_Unverified
data.comment: A value with its raw byte: {0} = the suggested name (e.g. Balanced), {1} = the raw byte in hex (e.g. 0xC1).

data.name: Wmi2_Raw
data.comment: A fan speed that cannot be worked out: {0} = the raw bytes in hex (e.g. 0x00 0x5A). Keep the dash.

data.name: Wmi2_Firmware
data.comment: Row name. EC = the laptop's embedded controller.

data.name: Wmi2_CpuTemperature
data.comment: Row name.

data.name: Wmi2_GpuTemperature
data.comment: Row name.

data.name: Wmi2_CpuFan
data.comment: Row name; the value is a percent and a speed (e.g. 45% · 3044 rpm).

data.name: Wmi2_GpuFan
data.comment: Row name; the value is a percent and a speed.

data.name: Wmi2_PerformanceMode
data.comment: Row name.

data.name: Wmi2_FanMode
data.comment: Row name.

data.name: Wmi2_ChargeLimit
data.comment: Row name: the battery charge limit.

data.name: Wmi2_CoolerBoost
data.comment: Row name. Cooler Boost is MSI's name for full fan speed: keep it in English.

data.name: Wmi2_FanAuto
data.comment: Fan mode name, as MSI Center shows it.

data.name: Wmi2_FanSilent
data.comment: Fan mode name, as MSI Center shows it.

data.name: Wmi2_FanAdvanced
data.comment: Fan mode name (a custom fan curve), as MSI Center shows it.

data.name: Wmi2_On
data.comment: Cooler Boost state.

data.name: Wmi2_Off
data.comment: Cooler Boost state.

data.name: Wmi2_StillRunning
data.value: MSI_ACPI: an earlier call is still running (it never answered); no call made.
data.comment: A WMI2 read is refused because the previous one never returned. MSI_ACPI is a technical class name, keep as is. Shown in the report and live-read windows.

data.name: Tray_Settings

data.name: Main_Settings

data.name: Settings_Title
data.comment: Title of the settings window.

data.name: Settings_TabAbout
data.comment: Tab header in the settings window.

data.name: Settings_Language
data.comment: Label above the language list in the settings window.

data.name: Settings_LanguageNote

data.comment: Small note under the language list.

data.name: About_License

data.name: About_OpenReleases

data.name: About_OpenLogFolder
data.comment: About tab button: opens the folder with M-Tool's log files in Explorer.

data.name: About_Copy

data.name: About_Copied

data.name: About_CopyFailed

data.name: About_Licenses

data.name: About_LicensesUnavailable
data.value: The license texts could not be read. They are in LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md on the GitHub page.
data.comment: Shown instead of the license texts. Keep the file names as is.

data.name: About_Unknown

data.name: About_Device_Model
data.comment: About tab device row label.

data.name: About_Device_Bios
data.comment: About tab device row label.

data.name: About_Device_Windows

data.name: About_Device_Firmware

data.name: About_Device_Record

data.name: About_Device_EcAccess

data.name: About_Writes_DryRun

data.name: About_Writes_Locked
data.comment: Changes row value.

data.name: About_UpdateHeader
data.comment: About tab section header.

data.name: About_CheckForUpdates
data.comment: About tab button: asks GitHub once for the newest release.

data.name: About_AutoCheck
data.comment: About tab check box: an automatic check a minute after M-Tool starts. Off by default.

data.name: About_AutoCheckNote
data.value: Only GitHub's list of releases is asked for; nothing about you or this laptop is sent. M-Tool never updates itself: the new version is downloaded from its release page.
data.comment: Small note under the update check box.

data.name: About_OpenReleasePage
data.comment: About tab button, shown when a newer release is out: opens its page on GitHub.

data.name: Update_Checking
data.comment: Update status while the check runs.

data.name: Update_UpToDate
data.comment: Update status.

data.name: Update_Available
data.comment: Update status. {0} is the new version, e.g. 0.17.0-beta.1.

data.name: Update_AvailableBalloon
data.value: M-Tool {0} is out. Its release page is in Settings › About.
data.comment: Tray balloon after the automatic check. {0} is the new version. Use the same words as Tray_Settings and Settings_TabAbout.

data.name: Update_CurrentIsNewer
data.value: This version is newer than the latest release.
data.comment: Update status for a development build.

data.name: Update_RateLimited
data.value: Checked too often. Try again in {0} min.
data.comment: Update status. {0} is a whole number of minutes.

data.name: Update_Unreachable
data.value: GitHub could not be reached. Check the connection.
data.comment: Update status: no network, DNS or proxy problem.

data.name: Update_Timeout
data.value: GitHub did not answer. Try again later.
data.comment: Update status.

data.name: Update_Unreadable
data.value: The update information could not be read.
data.comment: Update status: GitHub answered with an error or something that is not a release list.

data.name: Update_UnknownVersion
data.value: The version of this build is unknown, so it cannot be compared.
data.comment: Update status when the exe has no version (a local build).

data.name: Shell_UrlCopied
data.value: M-Tool did not open the browser, because it would have run with administrator rights. The address is on the clipboard: paste it into your browser.
data.comment: Warning band. Shown when the browser could only have been started from M-Tool itself (with its administrator rights), so it was not opened and the web address was copied instead.

data.name: Shell_UrlNotOpened
data.value: M-Tool did not open the browser, because it would have run with administrator rights. The address is in the log file.
data.comment: Warning band. Like Shell_UrlCopied, but copying the address failed too.

data.name: Session_PawnIoMissing
data.value: PawnIO is not installed, so Cooler Boost and the charge limit are hidden. To use them, install it (in an administrator command prompt: {0}) and restart M-Tool.
data.comment: SAFETY. Warning banner. {0} is the install command: copy it unchanged. PawnIO is a product name. Cooler Boost is MSI's name: keep it.
